_why: The whole US stack on one board — ingest jobs, the SEC service and the
realtime socket holder — because they fail as a unit and are scheduled on
the US clock rather than ours (11:00 IST for a 4pm ET close).
The seven job ids are the literal `job:` tag values their reporters emit:
Spelled out one series per job rather than a set filter: a `job:` value
that does not exist renders as a missing line, which on a board of seven
lines is far easier to miss than a whole empty graph.
title: UseMoney — US market stack
description: managed-by:apply-dashboards — edit the file, not the UI

definition.title: US jobs: upstream (transport) failures
definition._why: SEC answers a block with a 403 and a BODY, and Tiingo with a 429 — neither is a row that failed to persist, so neither shows up in `job.failed`. This is the only series on the board that can see an egress block.

definition.title: EDGAR detection latency p95 (s)
definition._why: The MONEY-979 acceptance gate is p95 < 300s. A DogStatsD histogram, so the sidecar produces the .95percentile sub-series; the base name carries no points.

definition.title: Realtime: healthy and leader
definition._why: Both are gauges emitted on every flush tick. A Redis leader lock at maxScale 1 is still required because Cloud Run overlaps revisions on deploy, so `rt.leader` briefly reading 0 during a rollout is normal and reading 0 for minutes is not.

definition.title: Candles written vs refused (mixed source)
definition._why: A refusal is CORRECT behaviour, not an error: one (symbol, timeframe, UTC day) may hold only one source, so a quote-derived realtime bar must not land beside a trade-derived EOD bar. A refusal count that goes to zero mid-session is the thing to look at.

definition.title: tiingo-realtime: hits vs errors
definition._why: Its own service rather than stockbook-workers, even though it ships in the same image: one long-lived process holding one socket, versus a request-driven pool. Blending them makes every percentile a mix of two workloads that fail in unrelated ways. `web.request` is dd-trace-js's SERVER span on the v0 attribute schema (`server.http.opName` in node_modules/dd-trace/packages/dd-trace/src/service-naming/schemas/v0/web.js) — here the /health liveness probe, on a bare node:http server with no framework plugin to rename it, declared in DD_SERVER_SPAN (packages/datadog/src/constants.ts; measured 2026-09-23, 2,876 hits in 24h). `http.request` is the CLIENT span, which charted this service's outbound Tiingo REST calls instead.
